consensus_summary: Babel/Babylon symbolizes proud, self-exalting human civilization organized against God, especially an idolatrous and oppressive empire or world system ruling over others and destined for judgment.
book_summary: Babel/Babylon is the self-created anti-heaven kingdom that seeks its own name, becomes an empire ruling other kingdoms, and counterfeits God’s covenant order.
consensus_core_identification: Proud human kingdom or imperial world order organized in rebellion against God.
book_core_identification: A self-made anti-God kingdom that develops into a dominant imperial and covenant-counterfeiting order.
boundary_disagreement: No clear material boundary disagreement is stated. The book emphasizes imperial hierarchy and covenant counterfeiting but does not explicitly exclude the broader consensus cases of prideful, idolatrous, oppressive civilization.
material_contradiction: None. The book’s self-made kingdom and empire are the same basic referent as the consensus’s proud anti-God civilization or world empire.
rationale: Reduced to their minimum cores, both identify Babel/Babylon with organized human self-exaltation against God expressed as a dominant worldly kingdom or empire. “Covenant counterfeit” adds theological characterization, but it does not replace the consensus referent or demonstrably alter which cases belong to it.
strongest_objection: Genesis 11:4 directly supports self-made fame against heaven, and Revelation 17:18 supports rule over kings; Jeremiah 51:7 supports worldwide corrupting influence. However, the specific claim that Babylon is a “covenant counterfeit” is not directly established by the printed excerpts alone.
